contentBlocks.text: This week you've learned how media is built, its purpose/audience, and its techniques. Today: analyze one complete example!

Read this complete social media post: 'BREAKING: New study reveals shocking truth about your morning routine — doctors don't want you to know this ONE trick! Thousands are already switching. Are you being left behind?' Write a short paragraph analyzing this complete example: identify its purpose and likely audience, and name at least two specific persuasive techniques it uses.
You just wrote a complete media analysis! Tomorrow we'll review everything from this week.

objectives: Combine purpose/audience identification with persuasive-technique analysis in one written paragraph
Write a coherent analysis of the complete social-media-post example
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review this week's how/purpose/audience/technique work together.
2. Read the complete social-media-post example together.
3. Have the child write their full analysis paragraph.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's cumulative review.
differentiationTips: Struggling: have the child answer three separate guiding questions (What's the purpose? Who's the audience? What techniques do you see?) before combining them into one paragraph
Ready for more: ask the child why a real reader might want to be especially skeptical of a post using words like 'BREAKING' and 'shocking truth'
This is the week's synthesis moment — combining all three analysis skills into one coherent written analysis is the genuinely important skill here
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is an open-ended analysis activity — check that the paragraph identifies the persuasive purpose and a broad audience (people curious about health/wellness content), and names at least two techniques such as loaded language ('shocking,' 'BREAKING'), emotional appeal (fear of being 'left behind'), and vague/unverified authority ('doctors don't want you to know').
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses Common Core Grade 9-10 RI.9-10.6/RI.9-10.8 together, synthesizing this week's three media-analysis skills before tomorrow's review.
